prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: production sheet sprite for Trick or Treat: Last Kid Standing
Input images: Image 1 = STYLE reference only. Image 2 = procedural LAYOUT guide only.
Primary request: Generate ONE asset. Match Image 1's world artwork and preserve Image 2's camera, canvas margins, silhouette scale, ground contact, footprint and orientation.
Subject: Isometric 2:1 (Diablo II / Commandos camera) hand-painted game sprite on a transparent background, Halloween night in 1990s American suburbia, cold blue moonlight from the upper-left, warm orange practical lights, clean painted edges, no ground/background, no cast shadow (engine draws shadows). A chunky toy-like twin-barrel mounted gun on a short tripod: candy-cane striped barrels, a purple round body and a clear hopper full of candy on top, rear grips. One row of 16 frames of 190x150px: frame 0 aims screen-right, then rotate clockwise in 22.5-degree steps (frame 4 aims toward the viewer/down). Pivot (tripod centre on the deck) at (95,100) in every frame.
Atlas entry: turret_candycannon. Mounted "Candy Cannon" turret on a tripod, 16 aim directions
Style/medium: Richly hand-painted stylized realism matching Image 1's Halloween suburban world: textured wood siding, slate shingles, weathered stone, fabric, metal, dense autumn foliage, softly modeled volumes and clear silhouettes. Smooth painted detail rather than pixel art or flat vector graphics.
Color palette: Deep navy and muted teal moonlit surfaces, rusty red and ochre autumn leaves, warm amber windows, orange jack-o-lanterns and practical bulbs. Preserve each asset's specified material colors within this palette.
Lighting/mood: Neutral moonlit exposure, cold blue light from upper-left, readable local material detail. Warm emission confined to actual windows, lanterns and pumpkin faces. Runtime supplies darkness, cast shadows, point-light falloff and fog.
Projection: Orthographic 2:1 dimetric projection. One native tile is a 128x64 diamond. World X goes screen lower-right; world Y goes screen lower-left. Visible building faces are +X and +Y; doors/porches belong on +Y (lower-left).
Canvas: native 570x900; render 2280x3600 (4x). If a different resolution is necessary, preserve the EXACT canvas proportions and all relative positions. Do not auto-crop or recenter.
Background: genuine alpha transparency; preserve fine edges. No painted transparency pattern.
Anchor: feet within EVERY frame at native (95,100), rendered (380,400). All contact positions stay fixed to the layout guide.
SPRITE SHEET: EXACTLY 3 columns and 6 rows of equal 760x600 pixel cells. No grid lines, labels, frames or borders. Each pose remains inside its own cell with feet at the same local anchor, no overlapping neighbours. Every occupied cell depicts the SAME character, body size, face, clothing and lighting. Preserve frame-by-frame pose movement in Image 2. Transparent gutters and empty cells stay empty. No weapon held unless part of the atlas design; runtime draws equipped weapons.
This is ONE 16 frame animation rearranged into 3x6 for generation. Read frames left-to-right, then top-to-bottom. The importer repacks it to the engine's original horizontal strip. Draw every frame; do not invent a different animation row.
Avoid: HUD, menus, screenshot borders, vignette, landscape/background, ground patches beneath props, cast shadows, atmospheric fog, bloom outside the silhouette, watermarks, invented text, clipped silhouettes, checkerboards painted into the image.
Output: one complete animation sheet of the requested character. No finished scene. Atlas geometry has priority over scene composition.
